host cell proteins are required in the synthesis of phage T4 DNA and for the synthesis of some structural phage proteins.

the characterization of a group of host mutations that have a pleiotrophic effect on bacteriophage T1 growth.
the role of the host cell during bacteriophage T 4 development.
the role of the host cell during T4 development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mutant host strains fail to synthesize sufficient rho factor to support the normal development of bacteriophage T 4.
the host mutations are in rho and that the pleiotropic effect of rho on T4 development is due to the absence of rho-dependent termination of transcription.
the host mutations block the expression of a phage gene or genes whose product is required for the synthesis of specific phage proteins and the initiation of phage DNA synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T4 phage genome contains a region that is essential for the development of the phage in the host cell.
the host cell is required for normal T4 development.
a single host gene product is required for T4 development and that it is a component of the transcriptional machinery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T4 host cell can be a limiting factor in phage development.
a host cell that is unable to propagate bacteriophages is defective for the expression of a number of early phage functions.
